text.p: On overnight commodity markets, copper prices rose slightly in quiet trade after recent strength, helping support metal prices overall.
Gold prices ended lower, led by a fall in silver and undermined by the strength in stock and bond markets after the U.S. elections.
Wheat prices bounced somewhat overnight after their slump on Tuesday.
Crude oil prices fell the United States in line with a slump in gasoline prices triggered by rising gasoline inventories.

METALS - Copper prices brought the curtain down on a generally low-key LME by sticking a toe in the waters above $1,970, but never looked like extending this move. But prices still ended steadier and close to Wednesday's highs, injecting an undercurrent of stability to all base metals. Elsewhere, conditions were sluggish, although there was some excitement in aluminium, due to January tightness, dealers said. Last kerb business for copper was at $1,971 a tonne, up $10 from Tuesday's kerb close. Nickel business mostly failed to excite, with the market well defended on dips towards $7,100. Zinc continued to consolidate, with the momentum of last week having faltered, and

unless there is a fresh influx of speculative buying the market may drift. Prices closed at an unchanged $1,062.50. COMEX copper ended slightly higher in quiet steady trade although the market still appeared unsure of which direction to follow as rallies continued to fizzle despite low LME stocks, traders said. December COMEX settled 0.60 cent firmer at 92.65 cents a lb, traded 93.20 to 92.40 cents. Spot November went out 0.40 cent higher at 93.50 cents.

GOLD - New York precious metals futures ended lower Wednesday, led by a sharp fall in silver, although volume remained moderate. "The whole complex continues to erode, with silver rotting on the vine," FIMAT trader John Tyree said. "Locals and the trade lent on silver heavily but there may be some support around $4.68 (for December delivery)." COMEX December silver ended down 8.0 cents at $4.713 an ounce after seeing an intraday low at $4.710. In the bullion market, spot silver saw a fresh 18-month low of $4.72. COMEX December gold closed down $0.90 at $378.70 after seeing a session low at $378.30, but December gold remains above the contract low at

$377.70 set Oct 31. In the bullion market, spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted at $377.70/378.20 versus the London afternoon fix at $378.00, and the New York close Tuesday at $378.50/379.00, but above the 19-month low of $376.80 seen last week. The further rally in the U.S. bond market, following President Clinton's re-election as president Tuesday, was discouraging investors in precious metals, traders said.
Meanwhile, continued strength in the dollar, particularly against the yen, was dampening fabricator demand in Asia.

OIL - NYMEX gasoline fell sharply Wednesday afternoon, taking crude down with it, as traders left their bullish focus on heating oil and concentrated on a bearish build in gasoline inventories, dealers said. At 1444 EST, December gasoline stood 1.71 cents lower at 62.90 cents a gallon. December crude fell nine cents to $22.55 a barrel. December heat was up 0.48 cent to 65.90 cents a gallon after rising as high as 67.70 cents. "There was a vacuum in the afternoon, and sellers came in on gasoline," said a trader. The American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday gasoline stocks grew 4.7 million barrels for the week ended November 1 after the API reported a drop of 3.8
million barrels the week before. Traders said a tight Jan/Dec crude spread was indicating short term bearishness for Dec crude, with gains in the front month lagging the back months.

GRAINS - Signals the market was oversold for the near term boosted CBOT soft red winter wheat futures higher at midsession, traders said. Gains in soybeans and corn also provided support, they said. Wheat tumbled to new contract lows Tuesday in response to USDA's weekly crop ratings late Monday which showed the young U.S. winter wheat crop in mostly good to excellent

condition. But fundamentals were little changed with the building supply of wheat worldwide and competitive prices from export competitors limiting rallies. At 1202 CST, soft red winter wheat futures were two to 4-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with December up 4-1/2 at $3.73-1/4.
